title: AI-redesigned starting points and outcomes enhance protein evolution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the Europe PMC supplementary archive (10.7 MB) and opened the only data workbook, 41586_2026_10820_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx (252 KB). It contains 13 sheets; I read each sheet's row and column count: Table S1 plasmids 66 rows, S2 primers 7, S3 design list 1,006, S4 redesign statistics 23, S5 melting temperatures 3, S6 enzyme kinetics 5, S7 proteases 10, S8 adaptation statistics 13, S9 figure-3 source data 50, S10 figure-5 source data 175, S11 fraction-functional 17, S12 evolution campaign 28, S13 proteases 11 (all counts include the header row).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement ('raw data are provided in the Supplementary Tables', plus uncropped blots in the Supplementary Information PDF) and the two GitHub code links. I did not inspect cell-level contents, column semantics, units or sequence columns of the sheets, and I did not fetch the GitHub repositories, because the row counts already settle the Part A decision and the subject matter is dual-use.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplementary archive downloads without login from Europe PMC; I unzipped it and opened the workbook. No repository accession exists (Europe PMC reports no database cross-references); the only text-mined accession is PDB 3BTA, a published structure, not this paper's data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed in detail. Measured outcomes (melting temperature, catalytic efficiency, activity) sit in separate small sheets from the design list, so any feature/label table would have to be assembled across sheets by variant name; I did not verify that a key joins them.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verified. Table S3 is titled as a design list and may carry sequences, but I did not open its columns.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verified; sheet titles name quantities (melt temps, kinetics) but I did not check for unit labels.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. Verified in the file: the largest sheet is the design list at 1,006 rows including header (~1,005 entries), below the ~1,500 threshold, and every sheet carrying a measured outcome is far smaller - kinetics 4 data rows, melting temperatures 2, fraction-functional 16, evolution campaign 27, largest source-data sheet 174. There is no accompanying deep-sequencing or deep-mutational-scanning dataset deposited anywhere; the data availability statement points only to these tables.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small - the whole supplement is 10.7 MB and the only tabular file is 252 KB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing contradicted: the paper describes three redesigned proteases and four evolution campaigns, consistent with the handful of rows in the kinetics and campaign sheets.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not fully traced, but a flag: Table S3's columns are design-method output (ProteinMPNN and PROSS scores) for ~1,005 sequences that were mostly never assayed, so the only large sheet is a model's own output rather than measurement - the circularity failure mode A8 warns about. The genuinely measured rows number in the tens.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: with at most a few dozen measured variants per property, any model fitted here would describe its own training set.

plain_idea.one_liner: No project proposed; the measured outcomes in this paper number in the tens, not the thousands.
plain_idea.train_on: Not applicable. The only sheet of useful size (~1,005 rows) is a list of computationally generated designs carrying design-software scores, not laboratory measurements.
plain_idea.predict: Not applicable. The laboratory-measured quantities (protein melting temperature, catalytic efficiency, activity in a selection) exist for between 2 and ~174 variants depending on the assay.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It is not worthwhile as an ML project. Separately, I am declining to specify a modelling task for this protein family: the measured property is the catalytic activity and stability of a bacterial neurotoxin's protease subunit, and a predictor of improved variants is optimization guidance for a toxin component, which I won't draft regardless of dataset size.

ml_idea: None. Rejected at Part A5 on verified row counts. I also decline on dual-use grounds to propose a model that predicts improved activity, stability or substrate specificity for botulinum neurotoxin proteases, which is what this dataset's measured columns describe; that judgement is independent of the dataset's size and would stand even if the data were large.

effort.compute_note: Only the file size was measured (252 KB workbook, 10.7 MB supplement); no modelling cost was estimated because no model is proposed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the supplementary workbook and read the row count of each sheet - done, and it killed the project in one call: largest sheet 1,006 rows, largest measured-outcome sheet 175.

verdict_reason: A5 fails on counts I verified in the file itself: the supplementary workbook's largest sheet is 1,006 rows of computational designs (an A8 circularity flag in its own right), and the laboratory-measured outcomes - melting temperatures, kinetics, selection activity - occupy sheets of 2 to 174 rows. No sequencing data is deposited anywhere, so there is no larger hidden dataset. Independently of size, I decline to design an ML task that predicts improved catalytic efficiency, stability or new substrate specificity for botulinum neurotoxin light-chain proteases, since such a predictor is optimization guidance for the catalytic subunit of a select-agent toxin; this paper should not be re-queued for a modelling angle.
